belief: Feeling angry is always a sin.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that feeling angry is always a sin, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A home where anger was frightening, violent, or forbidden. Being punished for showing any frustration as a child. Church teaching that treated all anger as sinful. Seeing anger only expressed in harmful ways. Trying to be “nice” at all costs, then feeling guilty when anger builds anyway.
teaches: Anger is an emotion God gave us, and it can be a right response to wrong. God Himself is slow to anger, but not without it. Jesus looked around with anger at hardness of heart. Scripture says, “Be angry, yet do not sin.” The question is not whether you feel anger, but what you do with it. Anger becomes sin when it is held onto, turns into bitterness, or is expressed in harmful ways.
self_statements: I’m sinning just by feeling this.
I have to stuff my anger down.
If I’m angry, God is angry with me.
errors: Believing anger is either completely absent or completely sinful.
Treating the feeling of anger as the same as acting in anger.
Assuming all anger is like the harmful anger you saw growing up.
Pushing anger down until it comes out in other ways.
questions: Did Jesus ever feel angry? Did He sin?
What does “Be angry, yet do not sin” tell me?
Is the problem the feeling, or what I do with it?
Where did I learn that all anger is sinful?
What happens when I stuff my anger instead of dealing with it?
Is there a wrong here that anger is pointing me to?
How can I express anger in a way that honors God?
truth: Feeling angry is not always a sin. Anger is a God-given emotion that can point to real wrongs. Jesus Himself was angry at hardness of heart. I can feel anger without sinning by admitting it, bringing it to God, dealing with it quickly, and expressing it in ways that do not harm others.
hw_questions: Did Jesus ever feel angry? Did He sin?
What does “Be angry, yet do not sin” mean for me?
Is the problem the feeling or what I do with it?
Where did I learn all anger is sinful?
What happens when I stuff my anger?
What wrong is my anger pointing to?
hw_truths: Anger is a feeling, not automatically a sin.
I can be angry and not sin.
Jesus felt anger at what was wrong.
I can bring my anger to God honestly.
I can deal with anger quickly instead of storing it up.
I can express anger without harming others.
log: Each time I feel angry, write what happened, what wrong I saw, and one healthy way I handled it.
name_example: Sarah can be angry, yet not sin; on her bed, she can search her heart and be still.
actions: Next time you feel angry, say calmly,
“I feel angry because ___,” to yourself or a safe person, instead of hiding it.
anything you are angry about and pray about it, so the sun does not set on it.
and write what Jesus was angry about and what He did with it.
when anger rises, then decide what to say or do.
tracker: One time I handled anger well
prayer: Father, thank You for making me with the ability to feel anger at what is wrong. Help me reject the lie that feeling angry is always a sin. Teach me to be angry without sinning, to bring my anger to You, to deal with it quickly, and to express it in ways that honor You. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
